body.text: Fri, 11 Sept, 7:50 pm, Final score, Rabbitohs 10, Knights 20
Rugby League World Cup live: Jillaroos 30-14 Fiji, Kangaroos vs Samoa semifinals
Australia moves to address its lack of forward pack punch ahead of its must-win semifinal against Toa Samoa after the Jillaroos shake off an early scare against Fiji.
The Jillaroos were caught cold by a red-hot Fijian outfit and trailed 8-0, but ultimately hold off the Bulikula to win 30-14 and set up a fifth straight World Cup final against New Zealand.
Follow all the action in our live blog below.

3' Samoa gets early advantage
Australia is pinged for offside and, as the bell rings for a set restart, Francis Manuleleua drops the ball cold, so it's a penalty for Samoa right in front.
They point to the sticks and Samoa will take the early 2-0 lead.
Interestingly, Jarome Luai has a chat with Ronald Volkman, who was kicking goals last week after replacing Chanel Harris-Tavita, and ultimately it's decided Stephen Crichton will be kicking.
He's got a heavily strapped left thigh, so I wonder will he only take the close shots and leave Volkman to try the tougher ones.
2' High shot by Tino Fa'asuamaleaui
Jermaine McEwen is furious as he's whacked high by Tino Fa'asuamaleaui, leaving the Knights back rower with a bloody nose.
McEwen is calling out the big Kangaroo, but he's off for an HIA.
1' Samoa kicks us off
And Tino Fa'asuamaleaui, who could have played for Samoa at this tournament, takes the first charge.
If this game is half as good as that pre-match, we're in for an all-time classic.
Teams face off in epic Samoan siva tau
Led by Junior Paulo, performed by 19 warriors and roared on by tens of thousands of fans.
And we've got ourselves a face-off.
This is as good as it gets.
Emotions running high
The tears are flowing for Samoa's national anthem, sung phenomenally by Deine Mariner's father, Lapi.
Ronald Volkman, Brian To'o, Junior Paulo ... the lot of them, just bawling their eyes out.
Here come the teams
The rain is hammering down and the wind is howling, sending the countless Samoan flags billowing as the teams take to the field for the anthems.
But first, a moment's silence for Paul Langmack, who died this week aged 61.
Some yahoos are shouting out during the silence, prompting a bemused shake of the head from Cam Munster.
The rain is starting to fall
If it's a damp track, the Samoans' big boppers could have the best of it tonight.
It's an SFS sellout
Tonight is officially a sell out with more than 40,000 fans expected.
Most fans are already in their seats here, and they've just been treated to an energetic light show.
There's a huge contingent of Samoan fans in here, flags flying proudly all over the stadium, but there is green and gold sprinkled throughout the stadium too.
And based off the noise factor with the team line ups being announced, it feels like there are more (or at least louder) Samoans in the house!
Is an upset brewing?
Are you a tad concerned about the Australia V Samoa game Jon? I know I'm not as confident as I should be for the Kangaroos to go through to the final.... - Mike
Are you a tad concerned about the Australia V Samoa game Jon? I know I'm not as confident as I should be for the Kangaroos to go through to the final....
More than concerned, I'm tipping Samoa to win this one tonight.

The biggest advantages I think Australia has are Jack Bostock aerially over Sua Fa'alogo, and Reece Walsh's ability to create something out of nothing (although Broncos fans have seen the flipside of that plenty of times).
But I have real concerns about Australia's forward pack against Samoa's, and the dynamism of the Samoan team all across the park.
LATE MAIL: Aussies get more punch through the middle
Our eyes now shift to the men's game, with the Kangaroos making a major change in the engine room as Keaon Koloamatangi replaces Pat Carrigan as starting prop.
The former Tonga prop will hope to give Australia some much-needed drive through the middle against Toa Samoa's fearsome pack.
The only late change for the boys in blue is the same one they made last week, with Jazz Tevaga starting at hooker in place of Benaiah Ioelu, who shifts to the bench.
About last night ...
We learned our first men's finalist last night and, despite Tonga's surge in the international game, it was the Kiwis who stamped their dominance on the game.
Fullback Kalyn Ponga was a huge difference maker in his miraculous return from a broken arm as New Zealand fired a warning shot to Australia and Samoa.
Tough contest exactly what the Jillaroos needed
After winning their three group games by a combined 242-6, the Jillaroos have at last been given a real game.
And, according to veteran centre Jess Sergis, it was just what the doctor ordered.
"I think that's what we needed," she tells ABC Sport.
"We knew what they were gonna bring. Their line speed, they've got big bodies and we felt that.
"We knew it was going to be a tough game and it's what we needed."
Sergis is nursing a bruised lip, a corked left buttock and just general soreness after a very physical outing.

Abbi Church was limping on full-time, Jaime Chapman is icing her left hamstring, and god only knows what the forwards are feeling. So the medical staff will have plenty of work to do heading into next week's final against New Zealand.
Key Event
FULL-TIME: Jillaroos are into the final with a 30-14 win over Fiji
What a performance by Fiji, but ultimately Australia's Jillaroos run out 30-14 winners at the Sydney Football Stadium.

Abbi Church is player of the match after her four tries and it's hard to argue with that, but Fiji five-eighth Luisa Yaranamua could stake a claim too for carrying the Bulikula so close against this almighty Australian side with her playmaking, running game, kicking game and defence.
70' The Jillaroos cruising home
After a surprisingly stern test tonight, the Aussies can at long last settle and jog through the finish line.
But the Aussies try one last attack down the right and Abbi Church is eventually brought down, and it looks like she may have hurt her left ankle as the siren sounds.
Hopefully that's not too serious, especially with Jaime Chapman also icing her left leg.
Nominative determinism at its finest
Poor Losana needs to change her surname! Look up what "lutu" means in Fijian 😬 - Lewa
Poor Losana needs to change her surname! Look up what "lutu" means in Fijian 😬
- Lewa
"To fall or drop."
That's a tough one for Losana.
Key Event
It's four tries for Abbi Church!
And this is the best of the lot.

Losana Lutu's bomb is well weighted to create the contest, but as Sienna Laing goes flying through (delivering a knee to the backside of Jess Sergis on the way through) Abbi Church maintains her focus to mark cleanly and then take off from just in front of her 20m line.
She beats one, two, three defenders, then freezes Cassie Staples with a brilliant left-foot step to go over for her fourth of the day.
Key Event
There's life in Fiji yet
Maria Paseka is over on the right wing after a lovely short-side play from the Bulikula, so the Jillaroos can't completely relax just yet.
I have to say, that try comes on the back of two shocking decisions.
First Losana Lutu kicked the ball straight into the ankle of Tarryn Aiken as she tried to tackle her opposite number.
Then Belinda Sharpe pings Simaima Taufa for ruck interference despite an exhausted Loren Ieli basically just dropping it cold as she gets up off the ground.
Regardless, the conversion from out wide is good for Luisa Yaranamua. It's 24-14 inside the final seven minutes.
60' A lucky break for the Jillaroos
The Jillaroos are going a little easier after establishing this lead but Fiji didn't get the memo as Luisa Yaranamua rattles Tarryn Aiken with a great shot.
It's called high, but I'm not sure she made contact with the chin of Aiken.
55' A rare miscue by Tarryn Aiken
Her previous cross-field kick had me wondering if it was too deep before Abbi Church arrived. This time, no such luck as the ball floats safely into Fijian hands for a 20m tap and seven-tackle set.
53' Jaime Chapman leaves the field
I told you earlier that Jaime Chapman was struggling with that left knee since an early twisting tackle.
It was good to see her come out after cooling down at half-time and get herself on the scorers' sheet, but now she's subbed off. Hopefully it's just precautionary.

Tiana Penitani-Gray is a world-class centre and Jess Sergis is similarly an elite winger, but interestingly it looks like Jess Skinner is sending TPG out to the left wing to keep Sergis and Abbi Church paired up on the right flank.
Key Event
What a try by Abbi Church!!

The cross-field kick from Tarryn Aiken looks like it might have just a bit too much on it, but the burst of speed from Abbi Church, who was in position for passing play, gets her there just in front of Tahlia Marshall.
Then the remarkable catch under pressure, and she manages to get it down all in one motion.
50' More pressure coming for Fiji
Jocelyn Kelleher goes to the line with the ball in one hand, shaping to grubber and eventually does. Isabelle Kelly is getting through and seems to be shocked that no-one from Fiji is diving on it.
Maria Paseka eventually gets there, and knocks on the ball around her ankles.
The Jillaroos are flexing
The fans continue to file in here, and you get the sense the Australians will go on with this one.

I don't want to write off the Bulikula yet, and they've been so good at maintaining that defensive intensity, but they've not had much of the ball in this half, and as soon as the Jillaroos get a sniff they're ruthless.
Jaime Chapman is in for Australia
The six-try hero from the triple-digit thrashing of Wales has been kept pretty quiet in this one after an early twist left her needing strapping on her left knee.
But, after a near miss with Maria Paseka juuuuust missing out on an intercept, Chapman dives in down a short left side with no room to move.
And Jocelyn Kelleher has found her radar with the boot, slicing low for a 20-8 lead.
43' Tarryn Aiken making things happen
The Jillaroos halfback is showing off her slick skills, this time chipping over the top and hunting for the ball.
She doesn't get the bounce, but Cassie Staples can't handle down around her knees and Australia goes right back on the attack.
Key Event
Abbi Church takes the Jillaroos back to the front
It looked like maybe the Roos had made another costly error, but Fiji got a finger to Olivia Kernick's offload. So the Jillaroos reset deep in Fijian territory.
Once again they spin it right and Jess Sergis's tap-on is perfect for Abbi Church, who steps inside three or four defenders to dive in.
38' Another blunder by Losana Lutu
Fiji's halfback is having a mare, with two dropped balls with her team surging late in the first half and now she's rolled a grubber dead for another poor end to a Fijian set.
Her poor performance is being driven home by the worldie being played by halves partner Luisa Yaranamua.
36' Jillaroos kick off the second half
Australia kicks long to start the second half, and immediately cop a penalty.
So Fiji is straight on the attack.
Samoa's Blue Army is coming
Hello from a chilly Sydney Football Stadium!
After the wild wet and windy conditions in Newcastle for the first men's and women's semis last night, it's looking a bit better here tonight.
It's pretty cold for November at 17 degrees (and a feels like of 11), but dry for now, although it is quite windy.
We've already had one game completed here, with Australia beating New Zealand 42-18 in the final of the Physical Disability World Cup.
A small crowd is currently in here, but as I was heading in there were so many Samoan supporters gathering in the neighbouring Entertainment Quarter for pre-match food and drinks.
The Blue Army will march into the stadium at 6:30pm, and I reckon they'll outnumber the Kangaroos' fans.
How are we feeling, folks?
Fiji are trying to bully Australia. Patience the beast will awaken... - Blake
Fiji are trying to bully Australia. Patience the beast will awaken...
- Blake
It’ll be right Jon. Early nerves . - Phillip
It’ll be right Jon. Early nerves .
- Phillip
I'm definitely nervous.
And torn because what a moment it would be if Fiji can pull this off.
Jillaroos not helping themselves
Fiji has absolutely aimed up, especially with their defence, and it's rattling the Jillaroos, who haven't been properly challenged at any point in this tournament.
But, with completions at 12/19 from Australia, not all of those errors are directly from Fiji's defence.

Yes, the pressure being applied plays a role, but now that the shock of that start is done, Jess Skinner can hopefully expect her experienced charges to get back to a more controlled performance in the second half.
That will be easier said than done though, especially if the likes of Luisa Yaranamua, Talei Holmes and Loren Ieli keep playing like they have done for the Bulikula.
All in the balance
What a great first half from the Fijians - well and truly testing the three-time defending champions who looked ruffled for most of that half.
Such is their class that they managed to ensure it's all square at half time with their ability to find the line despite very few forays deep into the Fijians' territory.
Fiji has enjoyed more possession at the break with 56 per cent, and have completed 80 per cent of sets compared to the Jillaroos' 63 per cent.

Halves Luisa Yaranamua and Losana Lutu have done a brilliant job of orchestrating things for their side, while some of Australia's biggest starts including Tamika Upton and Jocelyn Kelleher have had a bit of a mixed bag.
Key Event
HALF-TIME: Fiji running Jillaroos close at 8-8
What a performance from Fiji, taking it to Australia in a big way on both sides of the ball and the scores are tied as the teams head to the break.
This has happened to teams across the men's and women's World Cups with the question always being how long the underdogs can keep it up. But …
"The Aussie girls are blowing just as much as the Fijians right now," Cronulla fullback Jada Taylor says on ABC Sport.
Former Jillaroos prop Ruan Sims describes it as a "shock and awe" campaign from the Bulikula.
35' Fiji's last chance goes begging
The Bulikula is surging, but halfback Losanna Lutu knocks it on just as the shift to the left was building steam.
Huge let-off for Australia.
33' TRY-SAVERS FOR AUSTRALIA
Sienna Laing looks certain to score twice on the left flank, but the defence just cuts her down both times.
Tamika Upton and Shaylee Bent the heroes.
And now Upton bats a grubber out of the hands of Isabella Waterman to prevent a third potential try in a matter of seconds.
Jillaroos starting to switch on
The Jillaroos' completion rate after Fiji scored first was 40 per cent, with the visitors at 90 per cent.
Fiji has now dropped to 81 per cent, and it's provided a small opening for the Australians.
The Jillaroos still aren't playing their best, but will be buoyed by hanging onto the ball a bit more and finally breaking through for first points.
The Fijians look a bit tired and have started to give up easy metres, allowing the Australians to isolate defenders and break the line.
Upton's try could be an ominous sign, they are the best team in the world for a reason.
Key Event
The Aiken-Upton combo is humming and Australia is over again
In the redzone, this Jillaroos outfit is effectively unstoppable.
The remarkable thing about Fiji's performance so far is that they've so rarely allowed Australia to even get there, but now that they have made it again, Tarryn Aiken and Tamika Upton go to work.
Down the right, the former Broncos teammates create the extra number with speed and skill, and Upton skips outside Sienna Laing to dive over.
28' Here come the Jillaroos
A majestic ball from Tarryn Aiken unleashes Abbi Church again and, while the defence shuts it down, Aiken keeps the pressure on by rolling in a grubber and forcing a dropout.
Key Event
Slick stuff from the Jillaroos to answer back
OK, OK. That's a bit more like it from Australia.
An error from Fiji gives the ball to the Jillaroos and a penalty helps them out even more.
Keeley Nizza takes the quick tap to get them rolling up field and Kezie Apps makes the decisive charge to set up a right-side shift.
And the execution is flawless from Tarryn Aiken, Tamika Upton and Abbi Church as the Eels winger dives over out wide.
Jocelyn Kelleher can't convert, so Australia trails 8-4.
21' Changes for the Jillaroos
Jess Skinner has gone to her bench, introducing Kezie Apps, Keeley Nizza and Keilee Joseph.
They have their first really impactful set of the game as a result, with Abbi Church breaking down the right, but brought down by Taina Naividi and going within centimetres of being put into touch.
19' Jillaroos trying to fire back, but it's not working
Australia is trying to make the sort of defensive statement that Fiji has made early, but the over-commitment is allowing offloads and some quick metres through the middle.
Yet again the Jillaroos start their set on their own tryline and can't get over halfway.
I can't remember the last time I saw this happen to the Jillaroos.
FIJI ON TOP!
This has been a fantastic start from Fiji!

The Jillaroos have steamrolled all comers so far in this tournament, and while there's still a long way to go in this game, the Fijians have stepped up and are bringing incredibly defensive intensity, plus a sharp long kicking game to start this semi final.

They've been rewarded with forcing plenty of uncharacteristic errors from the Australians, and we shouldn't be too surprised that they've scored first since they've made a habit of making fast starts throughout this tournament.
The small crowd here is loving seeing a bit of a challenge to the women's international rugby league establishment.
Key Event
FIJI IS OVER FOR A TRY!
A bomb forces Tamika Upton to come from inside the in-goal. She somehow escapes, but the follow-up run from Jaime Chapman ends prematurely as Sereana Naitokatoka strips her.
Was it a knock-on? Perhaps, but play is allowed to continue.
A play the ball close to the line scatters defenders and Luisa Yaranamua throws a big dummy before diving over from the base of the ruck.
And she converts for a stunning 8-0 lead!
14' More like Bully Kula
The defence from Fiji is unbelievable right now.
Jocelyn Kelleher finds the sideline with her kick-off, giving the Jillaroos a perfect attacking platform.
But the defence forces Isabelle Kelly about 15 metres back.
Then Simaima Taufa is hammered by Loren Ieli, and then Tiana Penitani-Gray loses the ball on a short pass from Tarryn Aiken.
The Fijians are right on top here.
Key Event
Fiji takes a shock early lead
Simaima Taufa is penalised for crowding the play the ball and Luisa Yaranamua pots the goal to make it 2-0 to Fiji after 12 minutes.
It's the first time since the 2013 World Cup final that the Jillaroos haven't scored the opening points in any international.
9' Frustration from Jillaroos in the face of Fijian ambush
The kicking game of Fiji once again forces Australia to truck it off the tryline and the Jillaroos are struggling.
They won't be helped by a dropped ball from five-eighth Jocelyn Kelleher, who then cops a spray from the Fijians, prompting a bit of push and shove.
6' Another mistake forced by Fiji
The up-and-in defence from Isabella Waterman rushes Tarryn Aiken and forces another fumble.
Australia is under the pump early and Fiji's defence is aiming up to stop the Jillaroos from getting any sort of momentum too.
4' What a start from Fiji
Talei Holmes and Sereana Naitokatoka go within centimetres of scoring the opener for Fiji.
Credit the Jillaroos defence for denying them, but Fiji matches with driving defence to make life difficult for Australia getting out of their own territory.
3' Another chance for the Fijians
The Bulikula's first kick of the game is high out to Abbi Church, who decides to take it right next to the sideline before being dumped into touch.
She flicks a pass back in-field and it's dived on by Fiji.
2' An early error from the Jillaroos
A little bit of panic maybe from the Jillaroos as the rushing Fijian defence creates a dead end, forcing a u-turn and drawing the error from Millie Elliott.
Key Event
1' Fiji kicks us off
The second women's semifinal gets underway with Millie Elliott flying into the defence, followed by Simaima Taufa.
And then a big charge from Shaylee Bent earns the Jillaroos a penalty as Fiji is penalised for a strip. Can't be starting behind the eight ball against the Aussies.
The anthems are done
It's time for the Noqu Masu of Fiji.
One of the great pre-game traditions in world sport.
Here come Australia and Fiji
The Bulikula and Jillaroos are on the pitch at the Sydney Football Stadium.
How must the Fijians feel ahead of their first World Cup semifinal against the almighty Jillaroos?
Key Event
Kiwi Ferns in seventh heaven
No edition of the Women's Rugby League World Cup has been played without New Zealand reaching the final, and the Kiwi Ferns have done it again this time out.
The world number two reached their seventh straight decider, awaiting the Jillaroos or the Bulikula.
LATE MAIL: Jillaroos and Fiji 1-17
Tiana Penitani-Gray is returning for the Jillaroos in the back row after missing last week's win over Wales with a foot injury.
But neither team is making any late changes this afternoon.
Key Event
Welcome to the final four of the final four!
Hello and welcome to Semifinal Day II: Reckoning.

Today we learn who will join the New Zealanders in the men's and women's Rugby League World Cup finals, with Australia's Jillaroos up against first-time semifinalists Fiji and the Kangaroos meeting Samoa in a rematch of the last men's decider.
We'll have live coverage of both matches included some expert insights from Amanda Shalala and Nick Campton at the Sydney Football Stadium.
Stick around!
